blocks.text: ставить — поставить: to put, to place in a vertical position or on the base of the object; to park (a car). Phrases meaning direction are used to denote the place where something is put ("на" + Acc., "в" + Acc., etc.): *Я поставил лампу на стол. Я поставил автомобиль в гараж.* However, when something is put in a wide or open space, phrases meaning location are mostly used: *Я поставил автомобиль на площади.*
класть — положить: to put, to place, to lay in a horizontal position: *Я кладу книги в ящик. Я кладу книги на стол.*

садиться — сесть: to sit down. Literally садиться means "to seat oneself". It implies movement to a "seat" and, therefore, answers the question "куда?": *Садитесь на стул. Садитесь в кресло.* The same is applicable to the verbs ложиться — лечь (to lie down) and становиться — стать (to take a standing position).

The verbs "сидеть", "лежать" and "стоять" form their perfective aspect by adding prefix "по-": посидеть, полежать, постоять. These perfective verbs denote a completed action of limited duration: *Я хочу посидеть здесь 5 минут.*
From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lessons 42, 68.

The exercises are real sentences: from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR), with their English translations, and from the public-domain Russian books in this library, with author and title. The word in brackets is the dictionary form of the missing word.
